title: Collapse scattered localStorage keys into one versioned document with sync reads over async hydration
statement: Migrate N machine-local localStorage keys into ONE versioned JSON document in the durable settings store: hydrate once at mount (idempotent, promise-memoized, never rejects), keep the module API synchronous over the in-memory doc so no caller signature changes, write through with a debounced coalescing flush, do a one-time legacy import when the DB doc is absent, and degrade to a single localStorage key when IPC is unavailable. The storage KEY stays stable across doc versions — the version FIELD is what moves.

title: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never adds columns — pair every late column with an ignore-error ALTER
statement: On an install that already has the table, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` with a new column silently skips it — which is every install that matters. Additive columns need a paired `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` where 'duplicate column name' is treated as the success path, ordered before any index that depends on the column.

title: Wrap multi-statement DDL in an explicit transaction — SQLite autocommits per statement
statement: A migration batch of CREATE TABLE + CREATE INDEX + data backfill must run inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT; under SQLite's default per-statement autocommit, a crash or power loss mid-batch leaves half-applied schema that idempotency probes then misread.

title: Stage a column-to-child-table migration as numbered ADR steps: dual-write best-effort while the old column stays canonical
statement: To move data from a JSON column into a normalized child table without a risky cutover, dual-write during a transition phase in which the old column remains the canonical read source: child-table insert failures are logged and swallowed (analytics underreport, user data never corrupts), inserts are INSERT OR IGNORE for replay-safety, and each repo's create path calls one shared write helper. The ADR numbers the steps so 'drop the JSON columns' is an explicit later step, not an ambient hope.

title: Keep persisted values canonical English and translate only labels
statement: Persisted values stay canonical English; only labels are translated. A reason option is {label (translated), value (canonical, fed back to English-prompted scanners)}; preset sets live in code not the locale file ("data, not copy"), tested by localising the copy object and asserting the value does not move; templates use named placeholders because word order is not universal.

title: Link derived entities by index or identity, never by scanning display strings
statement: When one derivation pass produces parallel collections (triggers and the connectors that own them), carry ownership as an index-aligned or id-based link at build time — reconstructing ownership later by searching human-readable descriptions for a name cross-links every service whose name is a substring of another.

title: Close every author-chosen metadata axis, and delete the axis that cannot discriminate
statement: When many agents (or people) author metadata, an axis left as a prompt suggestion fragments into noise, and an axis whose instructions predetermine its answer returns one value forever. Ship each classification axis as a closed vocabulary from the single enforcing source, quarantine unknown values on an 'unsorted' shelf, and delete axes that measurements show cannot discriminate.

title: Give human adjudication its own timestamp, distinct from the row's updatedAt
statement: Any surface that windows on 'what was decided lately' must key on a dedicated decidedAt column set only when a human adjudicates, never on updatedAt — background maintenance (re-verification, taxonomy renormalization) touches updatedAt and would resurface months-old decisions as this week's news.

title: Stamp the scope baseline once at activation and derive scope creep from it server-side
statement: For any milestone/iteration cut, stamp a cut_at timestamp exactly once when the cut is activated, and derive 'added after cut' per member on the backend from membership time vs the stamp — scope creep then becomes a queryable fact instead of a retrospective argument, and no client can forget to mark it.

title: Normalize unzoned SQLite datetimes to explicit UTC before Date parsing
statement: SQLite's datetime('now') emits "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" — UTC with NO timezone marker — which `new Date()` misreads as LOCAL time, so a row written now displays as "2h ago" to a UTC+2 viewer. Detect the bare shape and append 'Z' at one chokepoint every timestamp formatter shares; pass through anything already zoned.

title: Encode the exact winning source into a discovered item's id; never re-derive at import
statement: When discovery resolves one of several ambiguous sources (GH_TOKEN vs GITHUB_TOKEN), embed the winner in the item id. Re-deriving from a category at commit time re-runs the last-writer-wins scan and can import a different value than the one the user reviewed and approved.

title: Persist an explicit empty value for 'user declined', reserving null for 'never asked'
statement: For optional configuration steps, save {} when the user explicitly skips, keeping null to mean never-prompted — later logic (nudges, defaults, re-prompts) can then distinguish a decision from an absence.

title: Identify the active version by an explicit tag, never by max(version_number)
statement: After a rollback, the demoted version still carries the highest version number. Selecting 'current' by sorting on version number re-selects the demoted version on every evaluation tick — an infinite rollback loop. Tag the active version explicitly (e.g. tag='production'), select by tag, and perform demote-all-then-promote inside one transaction so two rows can never both be tagged active.

title: Date.now()-only ids collide the moment a second writer or a same-millisecond batch appears
statement: `prefix + Date.now().toString(36)` is unique only while ONE writer creates at most one object per millisecond — an AI agent composing a batch in a single tick while the user is drawing breaks both halves of that assumption. Collision-safe form: base36 millis + per-process wrapping sequence (separates same-millisecond creations within one writer) + random tail (separates writers from each other). Leave existing ids untouched; only shape new ones.

title: Break intentional feedback cycles out of topo-sort by skipping designated edge types, and surface the rest
statement: Team/agent graphs legitimately contain feedback edges. Compute execution order with Kahn's algorithm over the graph MINUS a declared skip-set of edge types ('feedback'), assign layers as max(parent)+1 for layered layout, and treat nodes Kahn never reaches as cycle members: append them at the end with layer max+1, return them as an explicit cycleNodes set, and mark them visually — merged with any backend-confirmed cycle set — instead of failing or silently reordering.

title: Fall back from id-attribution to display-name matching only when the name maps to exactly one owner
statement: When attributing records to owners and the only remaining signal is a free-form display label, build the name-to-id map alongside a collision set, and use the fallback only for names that identify exactly one owner. A display label is not a namespaced key: two owners can share a name, and an unrelated system label can coincidentally equal an owner's name — silent misattribution is worse than leaving the record in the unattributed bucket.

title: Centralize a dual-shape reader for a field two writers shipped differently — scoped to that field only
statement: When two production writers persisted the same JSON field under different key conventions (camelCase vs snake_case), don't patch each reader with .or_else chains: create one tiny shared accessor that resolves both shapes with a documented precedence, and deliberately do NOT extend it to artifacts whose schema is well-defined — the dual-shape tolerance is a property of the one ambiguous field, and spreading it would mask real schema bugs.

title: Enforce late-added column bounds with ABORT triggers when ALTER cannot add a CHECK
statement: SQLite cannot ALTER a CHECK constraint onto an existing table; instead install BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE triggers that RAISE(ABORT) on out-of-range values, guard the DROP+CREATE behind a triggers-already-present probe (an unconditional recreate is a schema write on every boot), and rename the triggers whenever the body changes so existing DBs pick up the new definition.

title: Pair every settings key with a _DEFAULT constant and encode the unit in the key name
statement: A settings-key registry should ship each key with a sibling `<KEY>_DEFAULT` constant — so 'what does unset mean?' has exactly one answer codebase-wide — and encode units in the key name itself (`_DAYS`, `_MS`), with the rule that renaming the unit means renaming the key.

title: Resolve a config cascade once into per-field {value, source, isOverridden} provenance and render inheritance from that shape
statement: When effective configuration merges agent > workspace > global > default layers, do the resolution once (server-side) into a shape where every field carries its value plus which layer supplied it and whether it overrides the inherited one. The UI then renders per-row inheritance badges and inherited-vs-overridden counts from data instead of re-deriving precedence, and secret-typed fields are masked in the provenance view — including suppressing the hover tooltip that would otherwise leak the raw value.

title: Derive the value instead of storing a copy that can drift
statement: A stored duplicate of something computable drifts the moment one writer forgets to update it, and the drift is silent. Prefer a pure derived function, and treat not-known as a modelled state rather than a fabricated zero. Cache or store only when the derive is measurably hot, and then own the invalidation explicitly rather than hoping.

title: Leave unknown values unknown and report the gap to the user
statement: Interpolating a missing timestamp or estimating an unresolved price makes a dataset look complete while quietly corrupting every aggregate computed from it. Keep the unknown sentinel through ingestion and analysis, and surface the gap in plain language in the UI, so the reader knows what was not answered instead of trusting a fabricated number.

title: Compute catalog metadata from structure, don't ask authors for it
statement: Self-reported attributes like difficulty or setup time go stale and get gamed. Derive them from what the artifact structurally declares, using an explicit weighted score whose terms are individually capped so no single dimension can dominate, and snap the output to a few friendly buckets so the number reads as an estimate rather than a measurement.

title: Give repeatable analysis results a content-derived stable id
statement: Findings regenerated on every run need identity that survives the re-run, or any client holding a prior id — a debounced resolve, an in-flight fix — silently no-ops against the new result set. Hash the semantic content into the id and suffix genuine duplicates deterministically; a non-cryptographic hash is usually right for the collision space actually surfaced, and determinism also makes run-to-run diffing possible.

title: Store money as integer minor units and convert at one seam
statement: Float currency accumulates error the moment the database aggregates it, and conversions scattered across callers guarantee that at least one of them rounds differently. Let the store speak integer minor units so aggregation is exact, and put the conversion to and from display units at exactly one boundary module — the same move applies to any heuristic score crossing into a fixed-precision ledger.

title: Version every persisted document and sanitise it on read
statement: Anything persisted outlives the validation that wrote it: historical rows already hold values your current input rules would reject. Give the document a version, store machine tokens rather than rendered labels so it stays language-agnostic, and read it through a tolerant parser that coerces each field to its expected shape and degrades unrecognised values instead of throwing.

title: Soft-delete evidence rows and append rather than edit consent
statement: For records that may later be disputed — filed evidence, consent, chain of custody — an in-place update destroys the very history the record exists to prove. Soft-delete instead, keeping the row and its never-reused ordinal recoverable, and make a changed preference a new row rather than an edit. Conditional mutations should report whether a live row matched instead of throwing on a no-op.

title: Say so at the interface when two backends model a concept differently
statement: Behind one storage interface, drivers sometimes need genuinely different shapes — a relational child table on one side, an embedded array on the other. That is legitimate, but a reader who assumes a one-to-one mapping will extend only one side and ship a silent asymmetry. Document the divergence at the interface and keep a parity test, because nothing else forces both implementations to satisfy the same contract.

title: Add a thin promotion table rather than generalising a narrow one
statement: When failures live in several audit streams, resist widening one domain table to hold them all — its specific columns do not generalise, and every existing consumer inherits foreign rows. Add a thin table storing only promoted rows, keyed by a unique dedup key so promotion is idempotent at zero coordination cost, denormalise the display fields at promotion time, and normalise the sources' inconsistent severity vocabularies in one function.

title: Build a browse taxonomy from a scan of the real corpus
statement: A taxonomy designed from intuition orphans whatever the data actually contains. Scan the corpus, count the distinct values, fold them into buckets balanced against the observed distribution, and record those counts next to the definition so a later reader can re-check them. Add an alias table for the spellings the data really uses and a catch-all bucket, so nothing is orphaned or silently defaulted into a bucket that hides it.

title: Pin the source version at adoption so drift is provable
statement: Instances copied out of a catalog need to know when their source moved on. Stamp both the source id and its version onto the instance at creation; staleness then becomes a comparison rather than a heuristic, and the provenance also tells you what to detach on removal. An instance with no pinned version must never be flagged — a false 'update available' nag is worse than silence.

title: Commit to one SQL dialect so drivers never fork the query strings
statement: Supporting several database drivers tempts you to branch SQL per environment, and those branches drift until only one of them is really tested. Pick a single dialect every driver honours, resolve the driver once per process behind a cached accessor, and dynamically import each driver so unused ones never enter the bundle. Return a reason when nothing resolves — an opaque null is undiagnosable.

title: Consolidate every connection into one pool with one tuning point
statement: Modules that each open their own connection pool drift in exactly the settings that matter — pool size, TLS, statement timeout, schema sanitising — and the drift stays invisible until one of them misbehaves under load. Put the pool behind a single accessor that returns nothing when unconfigured, and let alternate embedded drivers implement the same interface rather than forking the callers.

title: Keep every SQL statement behind a repository module
statement: When one subsystem declares its schema inline and issues raw queries straight from command handlers, the data layer stops having a single edge — nobody can find, test or migrate that table with the tooling that covers the rest. Route every statement through a repository module even when the subsystem's storage model is deliberately unusual; the storage choice and the boundary are two separate decisions.

title: Validate settings keys and values inside the repository itself
statement: A generic key/value table invites typo'd keys and free-form values that no caller can be trusted to police. Keep the key vocabulary as named constants each paired with a default, encode units in the key name itself, and validate both key and value inside the repository's write path so no internal caller can route around it. Read paths stay deliberately more forgiving — warn and continue, so a legacy key surfaces in observability instead of returning a silent absence.

title: Register every feature's storage through one shared store factory
statement: Per-feature bespoke stores duplicate tenant scoping and each invents its own concurrency story. Define one factory that hands a feature a typed CRUD store, tenant-scoped on every call and backed by a real driver or an in-memory dev fallback — and give it atomic create-if-absent and compare-and-set primitives, so ledgers and state machines do not have to grow their own.

title: Make the client/server storage split a stated rule, not a precedent
statement: When some data lives in browser storage and some in a server database, the boundary is a real architectural decision — but if it is only visible as precedent, every new module re-decides it by imitation and the split slowly stops meaning anything. Name the classes of data each store owns and where the line falls, so the choice is looked up rather than guessed.

title: Compose the store interface from narrow per-domain repositories
statement: One flat persistence interface becomes a place any feature can reach any other feature's data. Compose it from narrow per-domain repository interfaces and have each feature narrow the shared accessor down to its own, so a cross-domain call fails at compile time. Cache the in-flight promise rather than the resolved value, or two concurrent cold starts each build their own database.

title: Select the persistence driver lazily behind one cached accessor
statement: Choosing a backend by config only pays off if call sites never see the choice. Resolve the driver inside a single accessor that dynamic-imports it, caches the in-flight promise so concurrent cold starts share one instance, clears the cache on rejection so a transient import failure can retry, and wraps the resolved driver with cross-cutting concerns once on behalf of every driver author.

title: Enforce the persistence boundary in the linter, then test the rule
statement: A documented boundary that lives only in a README is re-crossed the first time somebody imports the driver directly. Encode it as import-restriction zones — app code cannot reach a driver, persistence cannot reach auth — make every message cite the decision record so a blocked developer lands on the reasoning, and assert the rule's exact behaviour by running the real config against virtual file paths in a test.

title: Never cache a 'no driver configured' result — let late config heal
statement: Memoising the resolved persistence driver is right; memoising the absence of one is not. If configuration arrives after the first call — a secret injected late, an env var set by a supervisor — a cached null disables persistence for the whole process lifetime with no way back. Cache the resolved driver only, and re-resolve on absence.

title: Assign the store promise before the first await, not after it
statement: A lazy async accessor that awaits before assigning its cache lets two concurrent first callers both open the backend — fatal when the backend is a single-connection embedded database. Assign the promise synchronously and let both await the shared handle. Keep the composition itself thin: one file per repository, assembled by spreading them into one object.

title: Put all persistence behind one store interface and a lazy driver
statement: Six independent projects in this workspace converged on the same arrangement: a single store interface composed from per-domain repositories, with the concrete driver chosen by config and dynamically imported inside a cached accessor. Adding a backend then means implementing the interface and nothing else — no call-site changes, and no unused driver in the bundle.

title: Mine append-only logs incrementally with a per-file byte watermark
statement: Track a per-file byte watermark, spend a per-call budget reporting `exhausted: true`, and take first_seen_at from the real fs creation time — otherwise every row is born "today" and the 30-day dormancy guard can't fire for a month.

title: Parse timestamps to epoch before comparing when the backend mixes formats
statement: Never sort or cursor-compare timestamp strings lexicographically when the producer can emit more than one shape (RFC3339 'T...Z' vs SQLite-naive 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') — a string compare misorders the moment the two mix. Parse to epoch ms once, guard NaN, and pick the true oldest for pagination cursors regardless of display sort direction.

title: Keyset pagination over second-resolution timestamps needs a composite (at, id) cursor
statement: A timestamp-only keyset cursor silently drops rows when a burst shares one second across a page boundary. Make the cursor composite — the last item's timestamp AND id, exclusive — and thread both through the API. Related read-model honesty: push kind filters down into SQL so each source query gets its own limit (a chatty source must not starve others out of a shared union LIMIT), and compute facet counts in SQL because 'the facet rail cannot count rows it never fetched.'

title: Split SQL scripts with a lexer, never on semicolons
statement: Splitting a SQL script into statements requires a real lexer pass: consume single-quoted literals (with '' escapes), dollar-quoted strings, line and block comments, and track BEGIN…END nesting (triggers/procedures) — a semicolon is a split point only at depth zero outside all of these. Keyword detection needs word-boundary checks, and a trailing statement without a semicolon must still be captured. Pin it with a test file.

title: Exclude machine/correlator records from a recall window in SQL, so the window fills instead of shrinking
statement: Machine-written events (57% of the log) crowded conversation out of a 20-slot recall window down to 2 user messages. The fix is a writer-side marker prefix, one reader-side classifier, and a NOT LIKE fragment appended to the SQL — a post-filter in application code would just shrink a 20-row page to 8. The excluded records stay fully queryable through the audit read, FTS, and disk.

title: Keyset-page on a total order, and serve from the stored excerpt only when a shared cap constant proves it is complete
statement: Pagination cursors use (created_at, id) because same-second rows are otherwise orderable either way, which both skips and repeats rows at page boundaries. Hydration serves content straight from the SQL excerpt column when a shared cap constant proves the excerpt holds the whole body, killing a per-row file-read N+1 — the writer's truncation cap and the reader's completeness check are deliberately the same constant.

title: Result rows and run rows speak different status vocabularies — predicate on evidence presence, not a status literal
statement: When an eval pipeline stamps per-result verdicts (passed|failed|inconclusive) and per-run lifecycle states (generating|running|completed) into different tables, a WHERE status='completed' predicate on result rows matches nothing and silently empties every downstream rollup. Key 'is this a measurement' on the presence of at least one sub-score, and pin both the real verdict domain and the wrong literal in regression tests.

title: Push the filter into the query — a filtered page starves categories
statement: If a paged blended stream is filtered client-side, a chatty category crowds every other one out of the page and a low-volume lens renders empty even though thousands of matching rows exist. Push the filter into the query and cache per entity and filter, not per entity alone. Counts must come from the query too, and the filter vocabulary from a registry, so a value can be filtered for before an instance of it has ever loaded.

title: Give every list query a default bound, no exceptions
statement: One unbounded list query among bounded siblings stays invisible until the table grows: it reads and serialises every row on a path that was sized for a page, and nothing in review flags it because the code looks like its neighbours. Make a default limit part of the repository's contract, so an unbounded read has to be asked for explicitly.

title: Anchor time buckets on the data's own dates, not the client clock
statement: Deriving the current period from the local clock mislabels the head bucket whenever the client sits on the other side of the boundary from whatever bucketed the data. Anchor on the maximum date present in the returned series and do the arithmetic in UTC. The same discipline clamps negative age differences, so a future-dated row cannot slip past a max-age window.

title: Compare timestamps in the encoding the column was written in
statement: When rows are compared as strings, a cutoff formatted differently from the column silently mis-orders every row on the boundary — a separator that sorts after every digit classifies a whole day as older. The encoding is a property of the column, not of the language writing the query. Format the cutoff to match, or store both sides canonically; a retention sweep is exactly where a one-day error stays invisible until data goes missing.

title: Migrate stored settings forward, then deep-merge over defaults
statement: A version-keyed migration chain handles shape changes, but it cannot know about fields added after it was written. Wrap the payload as version plus data, run the chain forward, then merge the result over freshly-built defaults so any key no migration ever wrote backfills instead of crashing. Detect legacy unwrapped payloads by shape rather than assuming version zero.

title: Track applied migrations in a table and make the run idempotent
statement: If the apply loop reads a set of already-applied versions and skips them, running migrations becomes safe on every request rather than a startup-only ritual — which removes a whole class of ordering bugs in serverless and hot-reload environments. A migration may repair data as well as change schema: clean the existing bad rows and add the constraint that prevents recurrence in the same step.

title: Make each migration idempotent by probing the live schema
statement: A version counter records what you believe was applied; a schema probe records what is actually there, which is what matters after a partial upgrade or a hand-edited database. Model each step as a predicate over the live schema plus an apply function, and wrap the step's statements in an explicit transaction so a multi-statement batch is atomic even though idempotency lives a layer above it.

title: Upgrade a seeded user-editable file only on a stored version bump
statement: Files an app writes to disk and the user then edits need three rules: write only when absent, upgrade only when the embedded version exceeds a stamp persisted outside the file, and back up the previous contents under a timestamped name so a second upgrade cannot trample the first backup. Anything else either overwrites the user's edits every launch or freezes them on a stale template forever.

title: Copy the database file before the connection pool opens it
statement: An app that replays its whole migration chain on every launch mutates the user's data in place, so one bad migration strands it inside a half-migrated file. Take the snapshot before any handle exists — a plain file copy of the database and its sidecars is then consistent without any locking — make it best-effort so a failed backup logs and boot continues, skip it on fresh installs, and cap the retained copies.

title: Disable foreign keys before the transaction, restore with a guard
statement: Rebuilding a table to add a constraint the database cannot alter in place means dropping the original — which fires every other table's delete cascade unless enforcement is off. The pragma that disables it is a documented no-op inside an open transaction, so it must be set in autocommit first, and restored by a scope guard that runs on every exit path, because a pooled connection must never be handed back with checks off.

title: Bridge in-memory state cross-process via an INSERT-OR-IGNORE SQL projection with a TTL evictor
statement: The eviction IS the privacy bound — rows are post-redaction; writers sit one level above the cache so it stays DB-unaware; a cross-process round-trip test asserts a byte-identical rendered prompt.

title: Use localStorage as a deliberate, bounded, single-module persistence tier with an inline ADR
statement: localStorage can be a deliberate persistence tier when the ADR is written in the file (SQLite vs zustand-persist vs localStorage, with the repoint line) and every mechanic is tested: TTL, per-collection caps dropping oldest, MERGE-patch so two hooks own two halves, version mismatch discarded not migrated, corrupt read = fresh session. The journal is a bounded ring whose summary refuses to flatter (undone/conflicted excluded from throughput; median not mean) and markUndone AMENDS rather than deletes.

title: Use git itself as the per-turn snapshot/rollback store for agent-edited projects
statement: Instead of a bespoke version store, each AI edit turn commits best-effort (git add -A && git commit --no-verify, failures ignored), listing is one git log with a control-char field separator that cannot collide with commit text, and restore is git checkout <sha> -- . — files only, history preserved, next turn commits forward. Non-repo projects degrade to an empty list. Undo for ~60 lines.

title: Disk is the source of truth, SQL is a rebuildable index — and the FTS mirror is a contract, not an optimization
statement: Every memory tier writes markdown to disk first, then a generic node row, then a typed sidecar, then an FTS mirror. This yields crash-safety and a hand-editable rebuild-from-source corpus — but only if every new node kind performs all four writes: a kind that skips the FTS mirror is stored, looks perfectly persisted, and is permanently unfindable on builds without vector search.

title: Give user-writable data its own database file and pool, fully isolated from app state
statement: When agents or end users can run arbitrary reads/writes, host that data in a physically separate database file with its own connection pool, so no user query can corrupt or contend with internal application state.

title: Register connection-scoped extensions BEFORE the pool exists — they only apply to new connections
statement: SQLite auto-extensions (and any per-connection registration) affect only connections opened after registration; a pool built first holds connections that silently lack the extension, and every query using it fails on exactly those cached connections.

title: Stamp N parallel run/result table pairs from one declarative macro so every repo shares one CRUD and one status FSM
statement: When a feature grows N structurally identical mode tables (run + result pair per mode), generate get/list/update-status/update-progress/delete for all of them from one declarative macro parameterized only by table names, types and result ordering. The shared update_run_status reads the current status and validates the transition against one FSM before writing, so a transition bug is fixed once for every mode.

title: Prune dry-run by default, allowlist terminal states, clamp the age floor
statement: Data pruning defaults to dry-run, deletes only allow-listed terminal states (never NOT IN — an unknown state is never deleted), clamps the age floor, and makes destructive repairs an explicit second act.

title: Use a nullable-patch shape so omit and clear are distinguishable
statement: Model patch fields as `Option<Option<T>>` so "omit" (leave unchanged) and "clear" (set null) are distinct wire states.

title: Run conflict resolution as a second import pass over the same file
statement: Conflict resolution is a second import pass over the SAME file (the UI holds the path and passphrase); block a fresh import while one is pending, and merge the two passes' counters — sum counts, OR one-shot booleans — because backend counters are per-invocation.

title: A skipped tick advances the schedule pointer but must never stamp 'last fired'
statement: When a scheduler skips due work (outside active hours, gated, backing off), advance only the next-due pointer — writing the 'last triggered/fired' column on a skip makes the UI report a fire that never happened.

title: Derive a suppression-cache's retention cutoff from the largest live window, not a constant
statement: When pruning per-key state that consumers read over configurable windows, compute the retention cutoff from the maximum window currently configured across live rows — a hardcoded cutoff races any consumer whose window equals or exceeds it.

title: Rehydrate persisted sessions as an already-existing sleep state, not a new restore state
statement: When adding crash-restart durability to an in-memory registry, restore rows into a state shape the system already knows how to wake (here: a 'dozing tombstone' — displayed state preserved, no process handle), so the existing resume path resurrects them with zero special-casing and no new UI state.

title: Re-derive keep/delete from the user's resolution and assert they differ before a destructive apply
statement: When a conflict pair's A/B slots can be reordered by the model layer, resolve the user's choice into explicit keep/remove rows at apply time, assert they are distinct, and mirror the backend's refusal rules (pinned tier, cross-owner merge) client-side for a clear message instead of a generic failure.

title: Refuse an operation that would desync two stores; pair the refusal with compensation and a reconciler
statement: When a delete spans a relational table and a secondary (vector) index and the index is unavailable, error out inside the transaction so it rolls back — a partial delete leaves orphans that silently shrink every future result. Complement with create-side compensation ordering (build the easiest-to-roll-back store first) and a startup reconciler whose failed-check default is 'assume it exists, don't delete'.

title: In write-only secret forms, a blank input means 'unknown', never 'clear'
statement: Edit forms that never load decrypted stored secrets must submit only non-empty fields and rely on backend upsert-merge — sending blanks would wipe good secrets and hidden OAuth tokens the form could never display. Tell the user this in the UI copy.

title: Cancellation is a terminal sink: a result landing after Stop must never resurrect success
statement: Status finalization needs asymmetric compare-and-swap rules: only the cancel branch may write over an existing 'cancelled' row (to enrich a bare safety-net cancel with metrics); every other terminal status may only advance a still-'running' row. Without the split, a completion landing in the window just after the user clicks Stop clobbers the freshly-written cancel back to 'completed' — lost-cancel plus success theater.

title: Persist monotonic-clock state across restarts via elapsed-to-wall-clock conversion under a short TTL
statement: Instant-based transient state (an open circuit's opened_at) can survive restarts: persist it by converting elapsed time to an RFC3339 wall-clock timestamp, and on restore reconstruct the approximate Instant with now - elapsed (checked_sub, clamped to now). Restore only rows younger than a short TTL and purge the rest — stale transient state is worse than starting fresh — and treat every restore/persist error as best-effort (worst case: start clean).

title: Content-dedupe a debounced publisher by stamping timestamps at write time, not build time
statement: A snapshot publisher that debounces and skips unchanged bodies must stamp its publishedAt/updatedAt timestamp when the write actually happens — a timestamp inside the compared body would make every snapshot look different and defeat the dedupe entirely. On write failure, clear the dedupe memo so the next derive retries instead of believing the failed body was published.

title: Never write back a record hydrated from a lean list projection — re-read the full record right before the merge-write
statement: List endpoints often return lean projections with heavy fields blanked. Writing an edited record from a list row silently wipes those fields. The discipline: hydrate the full record per detail call for display, AND re-read it again IMMEDIATELY before any write ('the hydration map can be minutes old; another surface may have edited since'), merging the change into the fresh blob. When moving an owned resource between records, remove it from the old owner FIRST so a failed second write can never leave two live owners. Guard concurrent hydrations with a load sequence number so a stale response can't overwrite a newer one.

title: Rename a shared identifier atomically across every referencing store and return per-store counts
statement: An identifier referenced by several tables and embedded JSON configs (event types in events, subscriptions, trigger configs, persona prompt handler maps) gets renamed through ONE atomic command that: rejects reserved/infrastructure names, rejects collisions anywhere the new name already exists, updates every store in one transaction, and returns per-store update counts so the caller can show exactly what moved. Pair it with an idempotent one-shot cleanup command for the orphan classes that accumulate anyway (dead audit rows, missing auto-listeners).

title: Acquire every prerequisite before inserting the run row
statement: For invocation records (webhook runs, job rows), resolve everything that can fail up-front — auth headers, URL safety validation — BEFORE creating the DB run record. A failure during prerequisite resolution then surfaces as a plain error instead of a row orphaned forever in its initial status.

title: Classify each write as load-bearing or telemetry, and encode the difference at the call site
statement: In a long-running session loop, not all persistence is equal: checkpoint writes that downstream state depends on must fail the session loudly (update phase to Failed, emit the error, clean up, return), while telemetry/timing writes are explicitly best-effort and must never fail a phase transition. Encode the split syntactically — a persist_or_fail! macro for the former, discarded results with a 'best-effort, never fail' comment for the latter — so the classification is visible at every call site.

title: Forget by demotion through one shared statement that every read path filters on — never DELETE
statement: Superseding, size-cap pruning and status changes all funnel through a single demotion statement (importance -> 0), and every read path — list queries AND the keyword/BM25 lane — filters importance > 0. The record, its file, and its provenance chain survive, so forgetting is reversible and auditable; because the search lane honors the same predicate, forgetting actually binds instead of only affecting the list reads.

title: Sweep FK orphans at startup even when ON DELETE CASCADE is declared
statement: Declared cascades are necessary but not sufficient: crashed mid-flight runs and repo-bypassing code paths still strand orphan child rows. A one-shot, per-table, best-effort sweep at init cleans accumulated drift, no-ops on healthy installs, and logs per-table counts.

title: Seed vocabularies with INSERT OR IGNORE so re-seeding cannot resurrect operator changes; demote by status, never delete
statement: Boot-time seed rows keyed on a UNIQUE natural key via INSERT OR IGNORE are idempotent AND respect later human/agent edits: because the row already exists, re-running cannot reset a status someone changed. Removal is a status demotion, not a DELETE — a deleted seed row would silently reappear on the next boot.

title: Stage inbound sync deltas in an inbox table that exactly one reconciler consumes
statement: Cross-device (or cross-system) sync should never force-write long-term state. Land every arriving delta in a staging inbox tagged with its origin; a single scheduled reconciler is the only consumer, treats rows as semi-trusted evidence through the same dedupe/supersede machinery as local writes, and marks consumption with the consumer-run id (NULL = unprocessed) instead of deleting — giving idempotent redelivery and an audit trail for free.

title: Journal reversible writes as before-images through an allowlisted preupdate hook — and exclude tables where undo is a hazard
statement: For agent-write reversibility, capture INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on a curated table allowlist via the database's preupdate hook, persisting before-images (never after-images) through a bounded channel to a dedicated writer. Exclude the journal table itself (recursion), run records (undo must not erase evidence a run happened), and credentials (undo resurrecting a revoked secret is a security hazard). Store values as-persisted so encrypted columns journal ciphertext, and count channel-full drops as permanent, loudly-logged audit gaps.

title: Same-user device sync: three-way merge with first-class tombstones and a coordination-free deterministic tiebreak
statement: When both endpoints belong to the same user, a true divergent conflict can be auto-resolved by last-writer-wins instead of queued for manual resolution — but two things are mandatory. (1) If entities hard-delete (no deleted_at column), deletions must sync as explicit tombstone entries, because otherwise a delete on one device is indistinguishable from 'never synced' and the row resurrects on the next pull. (2) The LWW ordering must be a total order both peers compute identically with no coordination: later modified_at wins, and an exact tie (including unparseable timestamps) breaks on a stable device-id comparison.

title: A proposal queue against a moving target keeps exactly one pending row: filing a new one supersedes the old in the same transaction
statement: When an automated cycle files promotion proposals against an incumbent that keeps moving, insert the new pending proposal and reject any older pending proposal for the same subject (status='rejected', decision_note='superseded by a newer cycle') inside one transaction, so the human review queue never accumulates stale head-to-heads. Resolution fails closed (UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending', 0 rows = error), and the row carries the incumbent's base_updated_at so the human-approved apply can CAS against a target that moved since filing.

title: Upsert on a nullable natural-key column via a UNIQUE expression index over COALESCE(col, '')
statement: SQLite treats NULLs as distinct in UNIQUE constraints, so a natural key with an optional column silently duplicates. Build the unique index over the expression COALESCE(nullable_col, ''), write with ON CONFLICT(...) DO UPDATE that moves only the mutable fields (preserving the original id and created_at), and read back with the same COALESCE predicate.

title: Preview a cascading change, but let the backend decide the reconcile
statement: Before an edit that silently breaks other records, query the affected counts and require confirmation — and show no dialog at all when nothing is affected. Keep that preview strictly advisory: it is debounced and may still be in flight at save time, so gating the actual reconcile call on it lets a fast save skip rewiring consumers. The backend is authoritative and reports zero when there was nothing to do.

title: Recompute dependents on every write, and resolve them before a delete
statement: When another record's runnability depends on a shared row — a credential, a config, a licence — every create, edit and delete must recompute those dependents' derived readiness in the same command, or a run gate that should have blocked lets work execute against a dead reference. For deletes, resolve the dependent set first: the scan usually reads a column that vanishes with the row.

title: Merge partial updates in the database, never read-modify-write
statement: When several writers touch different parts of one document — autosave, an assistant suggestion, a second tab — an application-layer read-modify-write clobbers whichever sibling was written in between. Express the update as a single database-level merge of the partial input and implement it natively per driver. State it at the interface, because the wrong layer is exactly where the pre-read creeps back in.

title: Pair the age cutoff with a count cap, both scoped to terminal rows
statement: Age-based cleanup alone lets a chatty producer balloon a table inside a single retention window. Add a ceiling that trims the oldest rows, and scope both sweeps to the same terminal-status set — including the subquery that computes the keep window — so in-flight and dead-letter rows can neither be deleted nor consume keep slots. Default the sweep off wherever the data is unrecoverable.

title: Autosave by diffing a small derived slice, debounced, flushed on exit
statement: Persisting a long flow directly from its in-memory state writes constantly and writes stale snapshots. Derive a small persistence slice, skip the write when it equals the last synced one, debounce it, re-read the freshest state at write time rather than closing over a snapshot, and flush on unmount so closing a modal never loses the last edit. The in-memory reducer stays the single source of truth.

title: Refuse to save a config whose load failed
statement: A panel that falls back to empty defaults when loading fails will, on the next save, persist those defaults over the real stored config. Track load success separately from data presence and block the write until a successful reload, keeping a parse failure as first-class UI state rather than collapsing it into 'nothing configured'. When the config is a security policy, this is a security regression rather than an inconvenience.

title: Apply status changes conditionally on the status you expect
statement: A status update that does not name the states it may apply from lets a double-submit or a stale tab perform an illegal transition. Make the allowed source states part of the write, bundle any append-only log entries into the same operation so the log cannot drift from the status, and return whether it applied rather than throwing when a legitimate race loses.

title: Two flows that write the same columns need real mutual exclusion
statement: 'They operate at different levels, so they cannot conflict' is a claim about intent, not about state. Enumerate the actual writes: if two independent flows touch the same rows and columns they need a shared exclusion slot, acquired on every path and released on every exit. The precedence between all such strategies belongs in one documented decision tree rather than spread across call sites.

title: Separate incremental batches from full-snapshot syncs at the API
statement: A batch that is the complete current state of a dataset carries information a partial batch does not: whatever is absent has disappeared. Give the two cases different entry points so disappearance becomes a first-class detected signal instead of stale rows lingering forever, and make each caller state which kind of source it has rather than inferring it.

title: Select-then-insert is not an upsert — constrain it or serialise it
statement: A per-item 'check then insert' loop across pooled connections is not idempotent under concurrency, however idempotent the pass reads as a whole: two overlapping passes both observe absence and both insert, duplicating every row and everything derived from it. Either add the unique constraint and use a real upsert, or hold one process-wide lock for the pass. Startup plus a manual refresh button is the pair most likely to overlap and least likely to be tested together.
